justification: Extraction-pipeline config + one routing fix, no serving-path changes: (1) REPLACE the wrong Ashfield chapter-D manifest — it had 8 parts with locality-table names ('D-Part4 Haberfield' is actually chapter E2) and wrong page ranges, the root cause of the unreliable D-refs, missing Part 9, and bad auto-derived dcp_precinct_localities names; new 13-part table verified against the adopted PDF's per-page 'Part N' running headers. (2) ADD manifests for the 15 newly registered Ku-ring-gai Part 14 chapters (sections from each PDF's '14X.n' headings). (3) Add 'ashfield' to UPRIGHT_ONLY_COUNCILS (rotated 'Part N' side banner extracted reversed). (4) Hoist the #832 OCR fallback trigger into _maybe_route_via_ocr() called from BOTH extract() and extract_by_page_ranges() — before this, manifest-driven councils (all of Ku-ring-gai) never reached the garble check and kept doubled-glyph text layers.

pre_impl.existing_data: Chapter-D part list verified 2026-07-29 against R2 v1.1-2026-03-02 (13 parts, page ranges from running headers). KG Part 14 sub-parts registered same day via add_new_chapter.py (15 chapters, R2-mirrored). Review-mode runs (no DB writes) exercised every new manifest: round 1 exposed the reversed banner + missed OCR routing; round 3 confirms OCR now fires ('using OCR text for N pages').
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If KG republishes a Part-14 PDF with different pagination the manifest ranges drift — same exposure as every existing KG manifest; the r2_monitor hash-change flow re-flags the chapter.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Manifests follow the existing COUNCIL_CHAPTER_RANGES shape and KG one-row-per-section granularity. The OCR hoist moves an existing block into a method without changing its trigger logic; ocr_pages idempotence guard prevents double-fetch.

functions.name: _maybe_route_via_ocr
functions.input: self.pdf_path + council; env MODAL_OCR_URL/TOKEN; no args
functions.output: sets self.ocr_pages to per-page OCR texts when the raw text layer shows strong doubled-glyph evidence; otherwise leaves it None
functions.if_none: MODAL_OCR_URL unset or layer not garbled: returns immediately and extraction stays on the pdfplumber text layer, exactly the pre-change behaviour

functions.name: extract_by_page_ranges
functions.output: section dicts; now reads OCR page texts via _page_text when the trigger fired
functions.if_none: empty ranges yield an empty list as before; OCR fetch failure returns None and the text layer is kept (fetch_ocr_page_texts contract unchanged)

values.if_missing: chapter falls back to council-level page ranges or sequential detection — same fallback every unlisted chapter uses

queries: N/A - no SQL changed; the script's existing registry/provision queries are untouched.

break_it.scenario: A future re-extraction of any OTHER ashfield chapter now also gets the upright-only filter; a chapter whose legitimate body text pdfplumber marks as rotated would lose it.
break_it.what_happens: Text loss would surface as count_drop/schema_fail in the review gates before commit.
break_it.how: Review-mode round 2 ran the filter across chapter D: banner junk 0 hits, body text intact; gates block silent regressions for other chapters.
break_it.repro: Run --council ashfield --all --review and inspect the review file.

break_it.scenario: Modal OCR endpoint down or returns wrong page count during a KG run.
break_it.what_happens: fetch_ocr_page_texts returns None on ANY failure and extraction stays on the (garbled) text layer; the schema_fail artifact gate then blocks approval.
break_it.how: Existing #836 contract (exact page-count check) unchanged; gates remain the backstop.

break_it.scenario: The OCR trigger now runs for every manifest-driven chapter, adding a full-PDF text pass per chapter.
break_it.what_happens: One extra pdfplumber read per chapter (seconds); Modal spend only when garble detected.
break_it.how: ocr_pages guard makes it once-per-extractor; trigger requires strong doubled-glyph evidence per the #836 Sol-reviewed heuristic.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required — this PR changes extraction config only; DB content changes go through the review-gated extraction flow separately.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - reviews/ku_ring_gai_*.txt and reviews/ashfield_*.txt from the worktree runs; commit of extracted content is a separate deliberate re-run without --review after human review.
